title: the close gate skips L2/L3 on any test row carrying no file, counts it toward the pass, and never says so
body:
**THE CLOSE GATE SKIPS L2/L3 ON ANY TEST ROW THAT CARRIES NO `file`, COUNTS IT TOWARD THE PASS, AND SAYS NOTHING. AN ALL-LEGACY THREAD REPORTS `PASS 36/36` OVER ROWS THE GATE NEVER READ.**

Found and measured by **lamplight-vc** on Lamplight's canon; the mechanism re-driven here in Intent's source before filing.

## The mechanism, in this repo

`native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/contract.rs:681`

    if t.kind == AtKind::Test
      && matches!(t.status, AtStatus::Green | AtStatus::Red)
      && let Some(path) = t.file.as_deref()
    {
      if !refs.resolves(path) { ... }                       // L2: the cited file exists
      else if !completed && !refs.carries_id(path, &t.id) { ... }  // L3: it carries the AT id
    }

**The third conjunct is the defect.** A row with no `file` key fails the `let Some(..)` and falls straight through the block -- **no L2, no L3, no finding, no note.** It has already incremented `rows` and it still contributes to satisfaction. **The gate's own narrowing is invisible in its own output.**

## What that produces, measured on Lamplight (lamplight-vc)

    test rows, estate-wide:            1732
    carrying a structured `file`:       626
    LEGACY ARM, no `file` key at all:  1106      (64%)
    threads with rows in that arm:       78

    ST0286: 23 of 23 tests in the legacy arm, no `file` key in any of them.
    $ intent ac gate ST0286
    gate: ST0286 PASS -- 36/36 satisfied

**Nothing in that line distinguishes _36 checks passed_ from _36 checks had nothing to check_.**

## The corpus underneath is SOUND, which is what makes this a gate defect

Of the legacy rows, 850 name a path in their raw text; 337 distinct real-extension paths; **only 7 fail to resolve** -- ST0270 (4), ST0282, ST0286, ST0302 (1 each). Resolved by path suffix against `git ls-files`. **The data is fine. The gate's silence is the defect.** lamplight-vc reports two earlier passes wrong in opposite directions -- a prefix whitelist that acquitted 89 rows it never read, and a wide any-slash-extension match that over-accused at 95 -- and names the third as the one to trust.

## Intent's own estate has ZERO exposure, and that is the finding rather than the reassurance

    rows with no `file` but a `prose` citation:      45
    rows with neither `file` nor `prose`:            12
    of those 57, kind=test AND status green|red:      0
    rows WITH `file`, kind=test, green|red:         303   <-- the checked population

**So no row in this repo is silently skipped today**, and the 303 cross-checks exactly against the pre-commit `absent citation` arm's own report (_"examined 303 green/red row(s) with a citation, of 406 AT row(s)"_) -- two independent instruments agreeing on the same population.

**THE ESTATE THAT OWNS THE GATE CANNOT SEE THIS DEFECT IN ITS OWN DATA.** `legacy` rows are produced by the v2 migrator, and Intent was never migrated -- it is where the migrator was written. **This is the third defect today with that exact shape**: `0228` (five shell rules scope `bin/*` unconstrained -- invisible here because this `bin/` is all shell) and the `in-standards` decision-tree falsehood (invisible here because this project is Elixir-adjacent enough for the claim to look plausible). **A consuming estate is the only instrument that can see any of them, and none of the three is detectable by any amount of care applied from inside.**

## The contrast that makes the fix obvious

The pre-commit `absent citation` guard in this repo states its population in its own output: _examined 303 green/red rows WITH A CITATION, of 406._ **A reader knows immediately that 103 rows were not examined.** `ac gate` performs the same narrowing and reports only the pass. **The guard already demonstrates the correct behaviour in the same repository.**

## The remedy, as lamplight's hv ruled it

**An all-legacy thread reports `unchecked`, never `PASS`.** Small, well supported, and the general form is stronger: **the gate states its checked population the way the pre-commit arm already does**, so a partially-checkable thread is distinguishable from a fully-checked one.

## The prose and bare arms -- DRIVEN, and the earlier reading here was wrong

**Driven by lamplight-vc on Lamplight's canon after this issue was filed.** This section replaces an inference that said a `prose` row is skipped by the same third conjunct.

    arm      n      kind / status                                reaches conjunct 3?
    file     626    -                                            yes
    legacy  1057    -                                            yes -- 1048 gate
    prose     30    ALL kind=non-test, status=n-a                NO -- stopped at conjunct 1
    BARE      19    ALL kind=test, status to-write(16)/n-a(3)    NO -- stopped at conjunct 2

    prose/BARE rows that are kind=test AND green|red:  0

Control: the same classifier returns 1048 gating rows over the legacy arm and 536 over the file arm, **so it demonstrably reports a gating row and the zero above is the population rather than the instrument.**

**So neither arm falls through the `let Some(t.file)` guard -- `kind != test` excludes all 30 prose rows and `status not in (green, red)` excludes all 19 bare ones, before `file` is ever consulted.** The reading recorded here previously said the third conjunct skipped them; the drive says the first two get there first.

**AND THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: THIS ZERO IS CONTINGENT, NOT STRUCTURAL.** A `prose` row is not barred from being `kind=test`, and a bare row is not barred from going green. **The day either happens it lands in the fall-through exactly as described above, and nothing would announce it.** So: **mechanism confirmed reachable, zero instances in either estate today, and the exclusion is conjunct 1 or 2 rather than 3.**

**Intent's own zero is a DIFFERENT KIND of zero and the two must not be read together.** Intent was never migrated, so `legacy` rows cannot exist here at all -- that zero is structural. Lamplight's prose/bare zero is a fact about today's data.

## Not claimed

- How many other consuming estates carry legacy rows. Nobody has counted.
- Whether any estate currently has a `prose` row that is `kind=test`, or a bare row that has gone green. Both are representable and neither has been searched for outside these two estates.
